reason: Per-site verified (RFC 0106 wave 4b): schema_cache.rb:228-242 dispatches to `Marshal.load` or `YAML.unsafe_load` by extension; trails dumps and loads the cache as JSON (schema-cache.ts:134-146), so neither Ruby deserializer has a counterpart to call.

Per-site verified (RFC 0106 wave 4b): schema_cache.rb:79-89 may `load_cache(nil)` inline; trails' `isCached` is synchronous while `loadCache` is promise-returning, so the load is performed by `ensureSyncCache()` from the already-resolved dump (schema-cache.ts:839-842).

Satisfied by a different path: Rails' `columns_hash?(pool, t)` is `cache(pool).columns_hash?(...)` (schema_cache.rb:57), but trails' `cache(pool)` is async while `columns_hash?` is a sync predicate, so `SchemaReflection#isColumnsHash` calls the sync `ensureSyncCache()` analogue instead. `size`/`cache` in this file is the structurally identical omission (Rails `cache(pool).size`; trails `ensureSyncCache()` then `_cache?.size`), though that entry carries only the generic RFC 0047 seed reason rather than this explanation.

Per-site verified (RFC 0106 wave 4b): schema_cache.rb:441-445 calls `deep_deduplicate` to intern strings with Ruby's `-@`; JS has no string-interning primitive and identical string literals are already shared, so trails derives `columnsHash` only (schema-cache.ts:617-627).
Per-site verified (RFC 0106 wave 4b): schema_cache.rb:466 is `Zlib::GzipWriter.new file`; trails compresses with the pure `Gzip.compress` and writes the result, so no writer is allocated.

Per-site verified (RFC 0106 wave 4b): schema_cache.rb:246 is `Zlib::GzipReader.open(filename) { |gz| ... }`; trails reads the bytes and calls the pure `Gzip.decompress` (schema-cache.ts:149-156) — there is no reader object to open.

Per-site verified (RFC 0106 wave 4b): schema_cache.rb:69-71 is `cache(pool).size`; trails' `cache(pool)` is promise-returning while `size` is synchronous, so it reads the resolved `_cache` via `ensureSyncCache()` (schema-cache.ts:827-830). Tracked with the rest of the sync/async schema-reflection surface.
